subject: Bridgehead translation inconsistency causing large-payload failures (CentaurHealth)
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@centaurhealth.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@centaurhealth.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Problems after private cutover — large responses failing

Hi Vanessa,

We completed the private VPC cutover to the new on-prem edge (FortiEdge appliance) at 07:45 PT this morning. Since then some of our hybrid-app endpoints that call Redwood-hosted models are failing intermittently on large responses — we see TCP RSTs from the remote side and replays at ~MTU-sized boundaries. Small requests are fine.

Attached is a short pcap (pcap_bridgehead_gre.pcap) captured on the bridgehead facing the transit-gateway. We also included our infra diagram. Can you confirm whether Redwood has any MTU/fragmentation rules or SNAT path asymmetry that could explain this? This is impacting a couple of production flows (especially file-to-text ingestion).

We can jump on a call if helpful — ops@centaurhealth.com is on this thread.

Thanks,
Carlos Mendez
Sr. NetEng — CentaurHealth

--

Marissa / Karthik — looping you in. High level: symptoms (large responses break, small OK) point at MTU/fragmentation or SNAT asymmetry where return traffic follows a different path without state. Carlos supplied a pcap and diagram.

Immediate asks:
- Marissa: can you pull the Redis/worker logs for the Centaur tenant for the last 4 hours and check for observed socket resets / upstream timeouts?
- Karthik: please review the attached pcap for signs of DF (don't fragment) flags, ICMP fragmentation-needed, and whether return path IPs show different egress NAT IPs.
- Neha: if we need to open cross-account support with EdgeVendor for their FortiEdge NAT behavior, please draft — include the pcap and note that this is an asymmetric-return-path candidate.

Carlos — we'll triage and come back with a proposed mitigation (likely a temporary MTU clamp & pinning policy). If you can confirm whether the bridgehead appliance has any recent firmware changes (they mentioned a config push this morning), that would help.

I'll set a 30-min follow-up at 10:45 PT if we need realtime debugging.

—Vanessa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@centaurhealth.com>, EdgeVendor NOC <noc@edgevendor.net>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Problems after private cutover — large responses failing

Quick triage notes (from pcap and infra trace):
- I see SYN/ACK followed by data, then immediate RSTs at roughly 1460-byte boundaries. The packet capture shows TCP MSS advertised ~1440 and DF set on the server-side packets. No ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages are present in the pcap (might be filtered upstream).
- Source IPs from our inference pool show two distinct public SNAT IPs in different ASNs in the trace; return packets from Centaur go via their bridgehead to EdgeVendor, but some return traffic takes a transit path that rewrites source with a different SNAT (likely their HA pair). That creates state mismatch on path where conntrack expected the original NAT mapping.
- There's a clear MTU mismatch possibility: Centaur's bridgehead appears to be enforcing DF while path MTU is 1400 somewhere across the transit link (likely their vendor). For large payloads we get RSTs rather than Path MTU Discovery stepping down.

Suggested mitigations (short term):
1) Enable an MTU clamp on our egress towards Centaur's route (set MSS clamp to 1360) — short-term mitigation to avoid fragmentation-related RSTs.
2) Ask Centaur/EdgeVendor to check HA SNAT consistency — if their HA pair rewrites egress SNAT IP per node, we need consistent return path or state sync.
3) If EdgeVendor can permit ICMP type 3 code 4 through (for PMTU), that would allow correct PMTU discovery.

I can push a temporary MSS clamp on the Centaur model route if Vanessa approves. We should schedule a joint-debug call with EdgeVendor NOC to verify the transit.

—Karthik
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: support_bundle_20260814.tar.gz (logs + trace)
From: EdgeVendor NOC <noc@edgevendor.net>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, c.mendez@centaurhealth.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Problems after private cutover — large responses failing

Thanks for the packet capture. We reviewed the trace and confirmed the following on our transit fabric:
- There was a config push at 07:30 PT that adjusted ECMP nexthop selection for the Centaur bridgehead HA pair. One side of the HA pair is rewriting SNAT for outbound sessions when traffic exits via fabric node 11; the other node preserves original SNAT (we logged both behaviours).
- MTU on the fabric path between Centaur and Redwood peering is 1400. ICMP fragmentation-needed is rate-limited and was not visible in the capture.

Remediation plan we can enact immediately:
1) Rollback the ECMP change for the affected corridor (we can do this within 30 minutes) to restore consistent SNAT behaviour across the HA pair.
2) Allow ICMP type 3 code 4 on the corridor for a 4-hour window so PMTU can converge.
3) Provide a recommended MSS clamp of 1360 at the bridgehead (we can push this if Centaur approves).

We recommend Redwood apply the MSS clamp on your egress for a quick protective measure while we rollback. After rollback we'll monitor for 24 hours and then coordinate a controlled config push with consistent NAT behaviour.

Regards,
EdgeVendor NOC
